55+ TikTok Statistics You Need to Know in 2026
Last Updated: 6 February, 2026
TikTok has grown from a short-form video app into one of the most influential social media platforms in the world, with close to 1.9 billion monthly active users. For ecommerce brands and marketers, TikTok is now a serious channel for discovery, advertising, and direct sales through TikTok Shop. We've compiled over 55 verified TikTok facts and statistics with cited sources covering user numbers, demographics, revenue, engagement, advertising, and ecommerce data for 2026. Our research draws on the latest insights to give you the information you need to build a winning TikTok strategy.
Understanding TikTok's user base is one of the key topics when assessing the platform's potential for your brand. These numbers reveal a platform whose popularity has matured far beyond its initial Gen Z audience.
TikTok has approximately 1.9 billion monthly active users worldwide as of early 2026. Projections suggest it could pass 2 billion within the year, making it the fifth most popular social media platform globally. (DemandSage)
Daily active users sit at around 1.12 billion, giving TikTok a DAU/MAU ratio of 57.3%. More than half of monthly users return daily, a strong indicator of platform stickiness. (Backlinko)
TikTok has been downloaded over 5.48 billion times since launch across the Apple App Store and Google Play. In 2024, the app was downloaded 773 million times, making it the most downloaded app globally for the fourth consecutive year. (DemandSage)
Indonesia is TikTok's largest market with 180.1 million users, followed by the United States at 153.12 million and Brazil at 91.7 million. User distribution varies significantly by country, with other major markets including India (prior to the 2020 ban), Mexico at approximately 74 million, the United Kingdom at 23.4 million, and Canada at 15.1 million. (DataReportal)
In the EU, TikTok averaged 169 million monthly active users in the first half of 2025. European users represent a substantial and affluent audience. (DataReportal)
The United States is TikTok's second-largest market with 153.12 million users, reaching approximately 42% of the mobile population. With the recent resolution of regulatory concerns through the divestment deal, US user growth is expected to continue its upward trajectory. (Business of Apps)
TikTok is available in over 150 countries and 75 languages. Its counterpart in China, Douyin, has approximately 755 million monthly active users and operates as a separate platform. (Business of Apps)
The demographic composition of TikTok has shifted significantly since its early days, reflecting broader social media trends. The platform now reaches substantially older audiences with diverse interests, which presents new opportunities for brands targeting consumers with higher disposable income.
The largest age group on TikTok is 25 to 34 year olds at 35% of users. The 18 to 24 age group follows at 31%, representing a shift toward older millennials. (Statista)
Users aged 13 to 19 now account for 25% of the user base, down from 32% in 2021. Back in September 2021, when TikTok first hit 1 billion monthly active users, teens made up nearly a third of the audience. TikTok is no longer just a Gen Z platform. (DemandSage)
Users aged 30 and above represent 38% of TikTok's audience, up from 22% in 2021. The average user age has risen to 26.5 years globally, with regional variations: 28 in North America and 24 in Asia-Pacific. (DemandSage)
The 55+ age group has grown by 61.7% between 2021 and 2023. TikTok now reaches consumers with significantly higher spending power than in its early years. (DemandSage)
The global gender split is 54.5% male and 45.5% female. Male user growth has been faster recently at 31% year-over-year compared to 24% for female users. (DemandSage)
In the United States, 61% of TikTok users identify as female, which is the opposite of the global trend. Regional variations in gender distribution create distinct content and advertising opportunities by market. (Backlinko)
65% of TikTok users are aged 18 to 34. Among Gen Z specifically, 67% are active on TikTok, making it the dominant platform for that generation. (Statista)
How people use TikTok reveals the platform's grip on user attention. From creative filters to community challenges, there is always something new driving engagement. Daily time spent and interaction patterns show that TikTok commands more focus than any comparable platform, driven by its powerful recommendation algorithm.
The average TikTok user spends 95 minutes per day on the platform globally. This makes it the social media app with the highest daily usage, exceeding YouTube at 40 minutes and Instagram at 29 minutes. (Backlinko)
In the US, adults spend approximately 52 minutes per day on TikTok, while US teenagers average 87 minutes daily. The disparity illustrates TikTok's particular appeal to younger audiences. (Oberlo)
The average user opens the TikTok app 19 times per day. On Android devices, users spend approximately 34 hours per month within the app. (DemandSage)
An estimated 23.5 million videos are uploaded to TikTok every day, which works out at roughly 16,000 videos per minute. This volume of content creation keeps the platform continuously refreshed. (Buffer)
TikTok's recommendation algorithm drives approximately 85% of all video views, compared to around 57% for Instagram's Explore and Reels algorithm. This algorithmic edge gives organic reach far more potential on TikTok than on competing platforms like Snapchat or Instagram. (Sprout Social)
Average video length on TikTok has settled at around 42.7 seconds. Short-form content remains the dominant format despite the platform allowing longer videos. (DemandSage)
67% of users prefer brand content that features trending music, and 63% of high-performing TikTok ads communicate their message within the first few seconds. Creative approach matters substantially for advertising success. (Shopify)
TikTok's expansion trajectory has been remarkable and continues to make news, with growth persisting despite regulatory challenges in certain markets. Understanding this growth provides context for the platform's current dominance.
TikTok has grown from 271 million monthly active users in 2018 to approximately 1.9 billion in 2026. That is roughly a sevenfold increase in eight years, a growth rate far exceeding established social platforms. (Business of Apps)
In 2024, TikTok was downloaded 773 million times, making it the most downloaded app globally for the fourth consecutive year. Consistent top-download status reinforces its market leadership. (DemandSage)
In the first half of 2025, TikTok was downloaded 436.82 million times across the App Store and Google Play. Download momentum remains strong heading into 2026, though the platform remains restricted in markets like Russia. (DemandSage)
Audience growth in 2026 is projected at 17%, ahead of LinkedIn at 14% and Instagram at 13%. TikTok continues expanding its user base faster than established social platforms. (Backlinko)
Regulatory scrutiny in the US led to a potential ban in early 2025. In January 2026, a divestment deal was finalized, with TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC established under majority US ownership. ByteDance retained a 19.9% stake. (Variety)
Latin America represents 22% of TikTok's global reach with 356 million users, while Southeast Asia accounts for 18.7% with 298 million. Regional expansion continues to drive overall user growth. (DataReportal)
TikTok US Regulatory Update
The regulatory landscape for TikTok in the United States has been one of the most significant issues in tech policy, raising questions about user access and data privacy. Here is where things stand.
In 2024, a bipartisan law was passed requiring ByteDance to divest US operations or face a nationwide ban. A de jure ban went into effect January 19, 2025, though enforcement was paused through executive order extensions. (Variety)
In January 2026, TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC was formally established under majority US ownership. Oracle, Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi-based MGX hold 45%, eight additional investors hold 35%, and ByteDance retained 19.9%, just below the 20% legal cap. (Variety)
The divestment deal has resolved the immediate threat of a US ban. TikTok's US user base of 153.12 million is expected to continue growing, and the platform's commercial infrastructure including TikTok Shop is expanding rapidly. (eMarketer)
TikTok Revenue and Advertising Statistics
TikTok's advertising business has become a major revenue driver for brands investing in content marketing, with projections showing continued acceleration. These figures underscore the platform's value as a channel for reaching internet users at scale.
TikTok's global advertising revenue reached $23.58 billion in 2024, up from $13.2 billion in 2023 and $1.14 billion in 2020. This explosive growth demonstrates the platform's increasing appeal to advertisers. (Business of Apps)
For 2026, global ad revenue is projected to reach $34.8 billion, with forecasts suggesting it could surpass $50 billion by 2027. Growth trajectories continue to accelerate. (Shopify)
In the US, TikTok generated $11.01 billion in net ad revenue in 2025. Projections for 2026 reach $14.5 billion, representing approximately 38% of TikTok's global ad income. (eMarketer)
Advertising on TikTok reaches a potential audience of 1.59 billion people. The sheer scale of potential impressions makes TikTok attractive for brand awareness campaigns. (DataReportal)
Average CPM sits at around $9.16, with average CPC at approximately $1.00. These costs make TikTok one of the more cost-efficient platforms for reach. (Marketing LTB)
TikTok ads return an average of $4.13 for every $1 spent, compared to $3.21 on Instagram. Return on ad spend favors TikTok over established platforms. (Marketing LTB)
56% of advertisers report better performance on TikTok compared to other platforms. Majority advertiser sentiment confirms TikTok's effectiveness as an ad channel. (Shopify)
56% of US consumers have purchased products they first saw advertised on TikTok. The platform directly influences purchasing decisions across substantial consumer segments. (Shopify)
Brands running campaigns on TikTok see an average 26% increase in brand search volume. 45% of brands experience statistically significant brand search lifts after running TikTok ads. (Shopify)
TikTok ad CTR averages 0.84% with a conversion rate near 0.46%. If you're combining Shopify SEO with paid channels, TikTok should be part of that conversation. (Backlinko)
TikTok Shop and Ecommerce Statistics
TikTok Shop represents a fundamental shift in social commerce, offering new solutions for brands looking to sell directly through the platform. The growth in this channel has been extraordinary, positioning TikTok as a serious competitor to traditional ecommerce platforms.
TikTok Shop generated $15.82 billion in US sales in 2025, representing 108% year-over-year growth and a 407% increase from 2024. This acceleration is among the fastest in retail history. (eMarketer)
For 2026, US TikTok Shop sales are projected to reach between $20 billion and $23.4 billion. Projections exceed $30 billion by 2028. (eMarketer)
TikTok Shop's market share in US social commerce has grown to 18.2% in 2026, with projections of 24.1% by 2027. TikTok is capturing an increasingly dominant share of social commerce transactions. (Shopify)
The platform hosts over 15 million merchants globally, with more than 70 million products listed across 750+ categories. Product availability and merchant participation continue expanding. (CapitalOne Shopping)
In 2025, 71.4 million Americans shopped on TikTok, a 24.5% increase on 2024. Projections for 2026 range from 80.4 million to 94.2 million shoppers. (Shopify)
There are 171,000 small business merchants on TikTok Shop, accounting for more than one third of total transactions. Small business sales grew 70% year-over-year. (Shopify)
Beauty and personal care is the top-selling category at 18.65% of total TikTok Shop sales. Fashion and home goods follow closely behind. (Shopify)
TikTok's integration with Shopify allows brands to sync product catalogs, run ads from Shopify admin, and sell through TikTok Shop. For more, see our guide on TikTok and Shopify integration. (CapitalOne Shopping)
TikTok Creator Statistics
Content creators form the backbone of TikTok's ecosystem. Understanding creator demographics, earnings, and the types of content that perform best helps brands identify partnership opportunities and assess the value of influencer collaborations.
There are over 207 million content creators on TikTok worldwide. The gender split is approximately 64% female, 35% male, and 1% non-binary. (Influencer Marketing Hub)
Through the Creator Rewards Program, creators earn between $0.40 and $1.00 per 1,000 views. This is a massive improvement from the $0.02 to $0.04 per 1,000 views under the old Creator Fund. (DemandSage)
Finance and business creators see the highest CPM rates at $3 to $8, followed by technology at $2.50 to $6, and health and fitness at $2 to $5. Niche selection affects creator earning potential substantially. (Influencer Marketing Hub)
An estimated 100,000+ creators use TikTok as their primary source of income. US and Canadian creators receive 70% of net subscription revenue plus up to 20% in performance bonuses. (Influencer Marketing Hub)
Khaby Lame remains the most followed creator on TikTok with over 162.8 million followers. He is followed by Charli D'Amelio, Bella Poarch, MrBeast, and Addison Rae. (Influencer Marketing Hub)

Inside the rise of the top 25 most followed TikTok accounts of 2023, from Hollywood stars to lip-sync sensations

The face of TikTok had drastically changed in just a few years.
TikTok has changed immensely in the short time that we've known it.
The app — which skyrocketed to popularity after it merged with another platform called Musical.ly in mid-2018 — has developed a reputation for its distinctly Gen Z presence, and for lurching creators into the spotlight faster than most other platforms due to its algorithmic feed that doesn't rely on users following someone to see their content.
Young and previously unknown creators like Charli D'Amelio and Addison Rae gained mega-celebrity status on the app in its earlier era of 2019 and 2020, with short dance routines and lip-syncing videos that formed one of the platforms' most popular formats at the time.
Since then, the reach and relevance of TikTok have only expanded. Users of varying generations and with diverse content styles have found success on the platform — from mainstream celebrities like Will Smith and Dwayne Johnson using the app to promote their public profiles, to young comedians creating space for new and experimental comedy that is becoming hugely popular among viewers.
These are the 25 most-followed creators and accounts on TikTok right now.
25. Colombian singer Karol G has 43 million followers.
Karol G is a Columbian singer-songwriter known for reggaeton and Latin trap music. She has collaborated with many high-profile musicians, such as J Balvin, Nicki Minaj, and Becky G, across her career.
The artist, whose real name is Carolina Giraldo Navarro, has developed a loyal following of 43 million on TikTok, where she often posts short dance and lip-sync videos to promote her own music.
24. Indian creator Riyaz Ali has 45 million followers despite not posting in years.
Despite the fact that he has not posted on TikTok since 2020, 19-year-old Riyaz Ali has maintained an impressive following of 45 million followers on the app.
Ali is based in India, where TikTok was banned in 2020 after the country became involved in a geopolitical dispute with China.
Before the ban, the TikToker posted lip-sync videos using popular sounds on the app spoken in Hindi. He has since pivoted to posting more on Instagram, where he has continued to lip-sync to popular Hindi songs, and also posts lifestyle content, having amassed 27 million followers on the platform.
23. Former "Dance Moms" star Jojo Siwa has 45 million followers.
3 pulled muscles and a giant bruise later….
When she was just 11 years old, Jojo Siwa became a reality TV star on the cast of "Dance Moms," a dance show centered on students at the Abby Lee Dance Company in Pennsylvania.
Now, at 19 years old, Siwa and her mother Jessalyn have their own reality show, which follows the duo as they venture to create their own all-girls pop group.
On TikTok, Siwa often reflects on her time on "Dance Moms," recreating routines she performed on the show and reacting to clips from episodes that she was featured in.
22. Former Vine star Brent Rivera has 46 million followers.
25-year-old Brent Rivera rose to fame on social media by posting comedic sketch-style videos on the now-defunct video-sharing platform Vine.
He has since launched a lifestyle YouTube channel, where he posts challenges and vlogs, with 25 million subscribers. On TikTok, he often takes part in quick group games alongside his influencer friends and his sister, Lexi Brooke Rivera, who is also a popular creator on the app with 25 million followers.
21. Billie Eilish has built a TikTok following of 47 million despite only posting 16 times.
Grammy award-winning singer-songwriter Billie Eilish has only posted 16 videos on TikTok since she first joined the platform in 2020, but has still managed to maintain a strong following on the app among her fanbase.
Eilish's few videos on the platform have been very minimal in nature. She has previously experimented with popular filters on the app, and sung along to another creator who was playing her music on the piano on his account.
20. Former hairdresser Kris HC has 48 million followers.
Comedian Kristina Collins quit her job as a hairdresser during the pandemic and started posting videos to TikTok in April 2020, which paid off big time as she has since amassed a huge following, becoming Canada's most popular TikToker in 2022 with 48 million followers.
Her uploads often receive tens of millions of views each, and range from original comedy skits, to takes on popular TikTok trends and challenges, such as creating original album covers.
21. Kazakhstan's biggest influencer is known as HOMA, and has 48 million followers.
like my last post on instagram: hommm9k🥹
Kazakhstani influencer Alina Kim is better known by her TikTok monikers Homm9k or HOMA, under which she rose to fame with her lip-syncing uploads and trend-led dance videos.
Her YouTube channel has over 1.65 million subscribers and she primarily posts shorts that are similar in nature to her TikTok videos. She only has five video uploads, which include a vlog and a candy-themed mukbang.
20. Selena Gomez has an impressive following of 50 million.
On top of her thriving acting and singing career, 30-year-old mega-star Selena Gomez has a huge TikTok following, where she keeps fans updated on her Rare Beauty cosmetic line and latest music releases.
Despite announcing during a TikTok live in February that she would take a break from social media amid speculation of a fallout with Kylie Jenner and Hailey Bieber, Gomez has since reappeared on the app, sharing get-ready-with-me style make-up videos.
19. Younes Zarou's bright and colorful aesthetic has gained him 51 million followers.
@youneszarou Episode XIV: taking off to new adventures #yzfamily ♬ оригинальный звук - DOOMBREAKER
Germany-based TikToker Younes Zarou made a huge name for himself on the app thanks to his colorful videos which heavily feature the use of vibrant smoke, vivid liquid mixes, and splattering paint to create clever photo effects.
In February he officially hit the 50 million follower mark on his account and made a video to celebrate and thank his fans.
18. Dancer and choreographer Michael Le has 52 million followers.
@justmaiko back at it again wit the bruddaa🔥 dc: @notorlandolucas ♬ original sound - user93843045089
Dancer Michael Le's unique choreography and body movement helped him soar to the top of the most-followed list after he launched his TikTok account in 2016.
His popular videos frequently include collaboration dances as well as solo routines.
As well as showing off his moves, Le also shares behind-the-scenes recaps of his life, comedy skits, and challenge videos to his audience.
17. Kylie Jenner's Tiktok following stands at 52 million.
Reality-TV star, make-up mogul, cosmetics founder, and entrepreneur, Kylie Jenner has plenty of titles, and can add TikTok superstar to the list too.
The 25-year-old's videos often feature her brand "Kylie Cosmetics" which she launched in 2015, in the form of get-ready-with-me style uploads and make-up routine reveals, as well as cameos from very familiar faces such as Kim, Khloe, and Kourtney Kardashian, as well as Kris Jenner.
Jenner can also be seen taking on popular TikTok sounds with lip-syncing performances.
16. Korean TikToker Won Jeong has built a following of 53 million with his comedic reaction videos.
Korean TikToker Won Jeong established a massive audience on the platform thanks to his reaction videos, which see him respond to popular TikTok moments.
The content creator often recreates tutorials such as food eating tips and travel hacks, trying them for himself to see if they really work.
He also provides a comedic spin on videos that go viral on the app, such as recreating a scene of a woman dropping her phone, or a man attempting to walk on buckets of water, much to the delight of his fans.
15. TikTok star Loren Gray has 54 million followers and a fully-fledged musical career.
Told You So is officially out now 🪩🧸
Now 20 years old, singer Loren Gray started sharing videos on Musical.ly when she was 13, before it became TikTok in 2018. Her popular lip-sync uploads transitioned just as well to the new interface, and she continued to build her audience into the 54 million followers she has today.
Now a fully-fledged music artist, Gray has released a number of original tracks which include "Queen," "Piece of Work," and her 2023 song, "Told You So." In 2021, Gray was listed on Forbes' 30 Under 30 list as a result of her TikTok influence and the popularity of her music.
She continues to post videos on her account, which include teasers of her latest music releases, live performances, and lip-sync uploads.
14. Spencer X beatboxed his way 55 million followers.
This trend but beatboxified 🗣🧈🪰🦋
A self-described "Mouth music man," Spencer Polanco Knight, better known as Spencer X on TikTok, beatboxed his way to 1.3 billion likes and 55 million followers.
The 30-year-old taught himself how to beatbox back in his sophomore year of high school, and used YouTube tutorials to hone his skills, ultimately uploading original content to his own channel where he now has over 2.64 million subscribers.
Alongside his beatbox-themed comedy skits, challenges, and tutorials, he has also collaborated with fellow big names in the TikTok world which include Jason Derulo, Jake From State Farm, and Marshmello.
13. In addition to a thriving music career, Jason Derulo has 57 million TikTok followers.
In addition to a massive music career that includes Billboard-topping hits, 33-year-old singer Jason Derulo took to TikTok in 2015 with a dance routine challenge, and expanded his range of uploads to become one of the most successful content creators on the platform.
Derulo has an eclectic output that includes special effects edits, behind-the-scenes of those same uploads, comedy sketches, pranks, and challenge videos.
The performer has also collaborated with a vast range of creators which include fellow TikTokers Dixie D'Amelio, Frankie LaPenna, and Jo Lindner, as well as familiar faces from the entertainment industry such as Will Smith.
12. Dixie D'Amelio has 57 million TikTok followers, and has pivoted to a music and TV career.
Dixie D'Amelio is the older sister to Charli, who previously held the title of the most-followed TikTok star until June 2022. Dixie rose to fame around the same time as her sister, but steered away from posting dance content in an attempt to distinguish herself and pursue her own lane on the platform.
The influencer started off by posting comedic skits and lip-syncing content, and she has since built up a successful career in music as a singer, releasing her debut album, "A Letter To Me," in June 2022.
She also starred alongside her family in the reality show "The D'Amelio Show," which premiered on Hulu in 2021.
11. Korean band BTS has a following of 57 million on TikTok.
Superstar South Korean boyband BTS launched their official TikTok account in September 2019 with an immediate hit, delivering a simple filter video that was viewed over 136 million times.
Since then their semi-regular uploads have included dance routine performances, teasers for upcoming releases, and uploads of the members interacting and celebrating their achievements, such as eating a meal off their one billion streams plaque from Spotify.
10. Wrestler turned actor Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson can add "TikToker" to his resume with over 68 million followers.
@therock I just have oneeee more note @madametussaudsusa 😇😂@khloékardashian👊 ♬ original sound - The Rock
Former WWE wrestler turned Hollywood actor Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson is one of the most beloved celebrities on TikTok.
In 2021, audio of Johnson making his rap debut on Tech N9ne's song "Face Off" became a viral sound on TikTok, used by creators to make satirical memes about fitness and determination — a moment that he has become most-known for in relation to the app.
More recently, Johnson has shared clips of his workout routine on the platform, and he also took part in TikTok's viral "tortilla challenge" — where participants hold water in their mouths and take turns to slap one another with a tortilla in an attempt to make the other person laugh and spit the water out — alongside actor and comedian Kevin Hart, to promote "DC League of Super-Pets," a film that the duo starred in together.
9. Turkish chef Cznburak has 69 million followers on his account where he shares outlandish culinary concoctions.
Czn Burak Diet Burger Sever Misiniz?😂❤️🙈
Burak Özdemir, better known as Cznburak on the app, is a Turkish chef and restaurateur whose recipes and cooking videos have prompted a massive appetite for his videos on TikTok.
His viral culinary concoctions include giant burgers, fiery baklava, and elaborate fruit shakes, all delivered with his signature, unfaltering stare at the camera.
8. Actor Will Smith has 72 million TikTok followers.
Academy Award winning actor Will Smith's first TikTok dates back to October 2019, where he collaborated with special effects editor Caleb Natale to make his debut on the app.
Since then, he has dabbled in a wide variety of content, from further visual effects edits, to food preparation videos, gym workouts, and references to his notable film and TV roles.
In July 2022, Smith shared a series of videos answering TikTok comments from fans, following the Oscars controversy in which he slapped fellow actor Chris Rock.
7. Mexican singer and YouTuber Kimberly Loaiza has 72 million TikTok followers.

results.title: 46 TikTok Stats to Inform Your Strategy in 2026 | Sprout Social
results.content:
From viral challenges to Billboard hits, TikTok is where trends take shape. People discover brands, research products and even buy things directly on the app. The latest social media stats even show that TikTok has the highest engagement among all social media platforms. So it’s a must-have platform for brands that want to be a part of key cultural moments.
And for that, you need to keep a pulse on what’s going on in the platform. This means knowing who’s using the app, how they’re using it and how other brands are advertising.
Let’s take a look at the latest TikTok stats to inform your marketing strategy for 2026.
Key TikTok statistics you should know
Let’s start out with a few stats to highlight just how popular TikTok is with social media users.
1. Is TikTok the most popular social media platform?
TikTok may be popular, but it hasn’t surpassed platforms like Facebook and Instagram. In terms of monthly active users, TikTok ranks fifth in popularity. But when it comes to downloads, TikTok tops the list with 644 million downloads in 2025.
2. Is TikTok the most used app?
While TikTok has fewer users than other leading social platforms, it’s one of the most used apps. According to the Digital 2026: Global Overview Report, it has the highest average daily time spent per user.
3. Is TikTok the most engaging social network?
TikTok is the most engaging social network with an average engagement rate of 3.73%, according to Socialinsider. This puts it far ahead of every other platform, where engagement rates run below 1%.
4. Is TikTok the fastest-growing social media platform?
As new platforms emerge and user growth patterns fluctuate, TikTok is no longer the fastest-growing social media platform. But it still holds the record as the fastest social media network to reach 1 billion users.
Understanding these platform benchmarks is the first step toward building a sustainable presence, regardless of your company size. For leaner operations, translating these data points into an agile small business TikTok strategy is the most efficient way to maximize organic reach and drive revenue without an enterprise-level media spend.
TikTok demographic statistics
So who’s using TikTok? And is your target audience on the platform? Here’s a breakdown of the top TikTok user statistics.
5. Who uses TikTok the most?
According to the latest social media demographics data, TikTok is most used by male users aged 25 to 34 years.
6. What are the age demographics on TikTok like?
Based on the latest available data on TikTok demographics, here’s what the platform’s age distribution looks like:
Users aged 18 to 24: 30.7%
Users aged 25 to 34: 35.3%
Users aged 35 to 44: 16.4%
Users aged 45 to 54: 9.2%
Users aged 55 and above: 8.4%
7. What is the largest age group of TikTok users?
Users between the ages of 25 and 34 are technically the majority of TikTok users as the age group makes up 35.3% of the platform’s user base.
8. What is the gender distribution of TikTok users?
The same data source also shows that the platform skews male. 55.7% of the platform’s users are male and 44.3% are female. (No data available on other genders.)
9. How many Gen Z are on TikTok?
According to The 2026 Social Media Content Strategy Report, 72% of Gen Z users have a TikTok account. And as the earlier TikTok age demographics show, this generation makes up about 60% of the platform’s user base.
These numbers make it clear: TikTok is a Gen Z platform even if it has users across multiple generations.
10. Which country uses TikTok the most?
The United States has the largest collection of TikTok users globally, with 136 million unique users monthly. Indonesia comes next with 108 million users.
Marketers also need to look at how TikTok users are using the platform. Details like how much time they spend and what they do on the platform can inform your TikTok marketing strategy.
11. How many users are on TikTok?
TikTok has just over 1.99 billion monthly active users, making it the fifth most popular social media platform in the world. It trails behind Facebook (3.070 billion), YouTube (3 billion), WhatsApp (3 billion) and Instagram (2.580 billion).
12. How many accounts are on TikTok?
While there’s no publicly available data on the number of accounts on TikTok, a significant portion of social media users are registered on the platform. According to Sprout’s 2026 Social Media Content Strategy Report, 50% of social media users have a TikTok account.
13. How many daily users does TikTok have?
TikTok typically sees over 90 million daily active users in the U.S. As for global daily user data, the exact number is unavailable.
14. How many people in the world use TikTok?
More than 1.9 billion people in the world use TikTok. That’s roughly 23% of the total world population.
15. How many TikTok accounts reach 10k followers?
While there’s no data on the exact number of TikTok accounts reaching 10k followers, Statista reports on the distribution of influencer accounts by number of followers. In 2022, 33% of influencer accounts had at least 10k followers.
16. How many TikTok videos are uploaded every minute?
According to Statista, TikTok users are uploading 16,000 videos to the platform every minute.
17. How much time are users spending on TikTok per day?
Based on data from the Digital 2026 report, users spend about 55 minutes per day on TikTok. But in terms of average time spent per user, TikTok outranks every other platform. Each individual user spends about 1 hour and 37 minutes on the TikTok app.
18. How many times are TikTok users opening the app per day?
On average, users open the TikTok app about 10 times per day. This makes it the third most opened app after WhatsApp and Instagram.
19. How long does an average TikTok session last?
TikTok has an average session time of 9 minutes and 42 seconds. So it’s clear that those engaging short videos are keeping audiences hooked. If the average video is about 30 seconds long, users could end up watching about 18 videos per session.
20. Are users engaging with brands on TikTok?
While TikTok is a creator-driven space, users are still actively engaging with brand content on the platform.
According to the 2026 Social Media Content Strategy Report, 55% of Gen Z users engage with brand content on TikTok at least once—if not multiple times—per day. Another 30% of users engage with brand content at least once per week.
21. What are people using TikTok for?
37% of consumers use TikTok to keep up with trends and cultural moments. This TikTok stat from the 2025 Sprout Social Index™ reflects just how trend-centric and community-driven the platform is.
The platform is also inspiring purchases, especially among Gen Z users. 42% of Gen Z consumers turn to TikTok for product discovery.
TikTok advertising and marketing statistics
With TikTok constantly introducing new marketing and ad tools, the promotional possibilities are virtually endless. Staying on top of the latest TikTok marketing statistics will give you strategic foresight to build a strong brand presence on the platform. It will also help you run TikTok ads that deliver.
22. How many marketers are using TikTok?
Surprisingly, only 26% of marketers are using TikTok. With such big opportunities for brands on TikTok, more marketers should add this platform to their social marketing strategies.
That said, the platform is unique in terms of its content and presentation. This may explain why some marketers are still slow to get on board despite TikTok’s popularity.
23. Does TikTok see a high engagement rate?
Engagement rates on TikTok are significantly higher than on any other social network. As the Socialinsider data indicates, TikTok’s average engagement rate stands at 3.7%.
24. Is TikTok engagement declining?
On the contrary, TikTok engagement rate saw an increase between 2024 and 2025. That’s a 49% year-over-year increase. This is even more impressive when you consider that engagement on other platforms is either dropping or plateauing.
25. Are views declining on TikTok?
Similar to engagements, views on the platform are also increasing, albeit at a less impressive rate. The average views on TikTok jumped from 6,268 in 2024 to 6,496 in 2025 – a 3% increase.
If your videos aren’t getting enough views, it’s time to learn how to get more TikTok views and start seeing results from the platform.
26. How often are brands posting on TikTok?
In a sharp contrast to these high views and engagements, brands aren’t posting as much on TikTok compared to other networks. They’re averaging at 15 posts per month (or five posts per week).
27. When is the best time to post on TikTok?
While content moves quickly on TikTok, timing matters. Especially for brands and businesses.
According to Sprout Social’s research on the best times to post on TikTok, here are the key days and times to keep in mind:
Best days to post on TikTok: Weekdays
Best times to post on TikTok:
28. What type of content performs best on TikTok?
As expected, short-form videos are the biggest hit on TikTok. And the shorter the better. The 2026 Social Media Content Strategy Report notes that 60% of users interact with short-form videos shorter than 60 seconds.
For brands wanting to sell on TikTok, the platform lets you list your products and sell them using TikTok Shop. Getting a gauge on this in-app shopping tool will help you figure out just how effective it is and for which industries.
29. How many sellers are using TikTok Shop?
Red Stag Fulfillment reports that approximately 15 million sellers are using TikTok Shop globally. Among these, over 500k merchants are registered in the U.S.
Between steep discounts and countless affiliates on the platform, brands and businesses are seeing results from the app when it comes to direct selling. Brands should consider social commerce as part of their strategy, if they haven’t already.
30. How many users have bought something on TikTok Shop?
An estimated 870 million users are making purchases on TikTok Shop. And a survey from PartnerCentric notes that 37% of Americans under 60 have purchased something on TikTok Shop. These buyers are spending an average of $700 across 12 purchases.
As these numbers indicate, TikTok Shop isn’t a niche feature of the platform anymore. Users are actively using it because:
It’s easy to purchase (49%)
Item is/was on sale (39%)
31. What are the most popular categories on TikTok Shop?
Beauty and personal care is the most popular category on TikTok Shop, selling 370 million units worldwide in 2024. Womenswear and underwear is another popular category, with nearly 285 million units sold.
Meanwhile, the most popular purchases according to the PartnerCentric survey were: personal accessories (46%), household items (43%) and fashion items (40%).
32. Is TikTok Shop driving impulse purchases?
Nearly one out of four consumers makes impulse purchases on TikTok Shop. This makes sense because users get to buy an item immediately after discovering it. And a shorter buying journey translates to more impulse buys.
33. How much in sales does TikTok Shop generate?
eMarketer reports that TikTok Shop reached $15.82 billion in U.S sales in 2025. So it now accounts for 18.2% of social commerce in the U.S.
34. How many TikTok Shops reach $1 million in GMV?
The Red Stag Fulfillment data notes that 1,033 TikTok Shops in the U.S exceeded $1 million in annual gross merchant value (GMV). Meanwhile, fewer than 100 (77) Shops surpassed the $10 million mark.
TikTok for business stats
So should your brand be on TikTok? And how can it show up for consumers on the platform? Understanding how to use TikTok for business and reach your target audience is essential to success on the network.
35. Is TikTok a good platform for product discovery?
As the earlier TikTok user statistics show, people are regularly engaging with brands on the platform.
While there are plenty of reasons to use TikTok, the app has earned its status as a shopping hub. According to data from Sprout’s 2026 Content Strategy Report, TikTok is the top channel for product discovery among Gen Z.
36. Is TikTok driving direct purchases?
According to the 2025 Sprout Social Index™, when consumers are ready to make a direct purchase, they are most likely to turn to Facebook, followed by TikTok and Instagram. 36% of direct purchases via social were on TikTok. Gen Z and Millennials are more likely to turn to TikTok at 54% and 47%, respectively.
37. Are people influenced by TikTok ads?
The previously cited PartnerCentric survey found that 25% of users who bought from TikTok Shop found the item through a TikTok ad. This shows that advertising on TikTok is highly impactful, especially with strategic targeting and persuasive ad creative.
38. How much revenue does TikTok generate?
TikTok’s revenue has been growing at a notable pace. In the fourth quarter of 2025 alone, it generated about $1.3 billion in revenue from in-app purchases. This includes revenue from virtual gifts, advertising and ecommerce sales.
39. How much revenue does TikTok generate from advertising?
TikTok’s ad revenue through initiatives such as TikTok Promote and TikTok Shop have been successful, with a projected $34.8 billion in projected ad revenue by 2026.
With TikTok being a creator-driven platform, TikTok influencers can take your marketing to the next level.
Let’s look at some key influencer marketing stats relevant to the platform.
40. What’s the average engagement rate for TikTok influencers?
According to data from Sprout Social Influencer Marketing (formerly Tagger), the average engagement rate per post for a TikTok influencer is 1.86%. Here’s a breakdown on what those posts cost depending on the size of the influencer’s audience:

TikTok Statistics for Marketers in 2026

by Dayna WinterJul 29, 2026 • 10 min read
If your business is trying to reach people aged 34 and younger, chances are you’re already using TikTok. If not, it’s time to consider how this social media platform could fit into your marketing strategy.
One of the fastest-growing and most-downloaded social apps on the planet, TikTok is the place where trends are born, stars are made, and the hottest products sell out in minutes. Brands that understand TikTok trends and the unique content that succeeds on the platform can achieve positive return on ad spend (ROAS) and—better yet—virality with their organic content.
Not sure if TikTok is right for you or your brand? Dive into the latest TikTok usage statistics to understand the platform’s audience, average time spent on the app, and why partnering with TikTok creators can be a smart influencer marketing tactic.
TikTok statistics for brands and marketers
The following TikTok statistics cover a number of topics, including TikTok audience demographics statistics, TikTok for ecommerce, TikTok ads and ROI, and how the social media platform stacks up against rivals:
1. How many people are on TikTok?
In 2026, TikTok is forecasted to reach approximately 1.54 billion global users. The platform joins a handful of other social media apps that have crossed a billion users.
TikTok’s ascent to this milestone was faster than most—the company reached the 1 billion mark in 2021, less than five years after its 2016 launch. In total time to reach 1 billion, the TikTok app takes second place by a slim margin, behind Meta’s Facebook Messenger app. Competitors like WeChat, Instagram, and YouTube each took seven or more years to achieve the same numbers.
2. What is the total number of TikTok downloads?
The total number of TikTok downloads is more than 6.1 billion cumulative downloads.
Launched in 2017 as the international version of Chinese-developed social media Douyin, TikTok’s popularity skyrocketed in 2020 during the COVID-19 pandemic lockdowns, reaching a peak of approximately 313.5 million downloads during the first quarter of the year. Since then, the app has experienced steady growth, with more than 1.6 billion downloads combined in 2024 and 2025.
Here’s how it grew in the most recently reported quarters, in millions:
3. How much is TikTok expected to grow?
The popular social media platform is forecasted to reach approximately 1.9 billion users by 2029.
4. What are the age demographics of TikTok users?
TikTok has high adoption among Gen Z and younger, but other demographics are also increasingly using the platform.
The majority of TikTok users are 18 and older, which is important to note because these are the TikTok users brands can advertise to (the minimum user age is 13, but TikTok ads can only be shown to users over 18).
But how does the user age breakdown look among those over 18? TikTok users over 18 fell into the following age brackets.
18 to 24: 23.5% of TikTok users over 18
25 to 34: 41.6% of TikTok users over 18
35 to 44: 16.8% of TikTok users over 18
45 to 54: 9.3% of TikTok users over 18
55 and older: 8.9% of TikTok users over 18
While it’s clear Gen Z users dominate the platform, there is increasing usage among older generations. Over the course of a year, usage rose from 7.9% to 9.2% for 45- to 54-year-olds and 6.2% to 8.4% for those 55 and older. This could be a signal that brands with older target audiences should consider the platform when developing their TikTok marketing strategies.

5. What are TikTok’s gender demographics?
As of October 2025, TikTok’s distribution of gender identification among users was as follows:
45.5% of TikTok users identified as female
54.5% of TikTok users identified as male
This points to an opportunity for brands with a male target audience to advertise on TikTok.
This study did not include other gender representations, such as nonbinary. According to the most recent available surveying, around 5% of young adults (under 30) in the US identify as trans or nonbinary, compared to 1.6% of the general US adult population. Mapping this data against TikTok’s own user demographics indicates the gender data above may be incomplete.
That said, TikTok has attempted to position itself as a safe space for queer expression and gender expression, banning misgendering and deadnaming from TikTok videos and comments in 2022. If your brand aims to connect with a younger LGBTQ+ community, TikTok may be the place to reach them.
6. In which countries is TikTok most popular?
Although 19 countries have banned TikTok, the app has gained global traction. As of 2025, the countries with the most active TikTok users (over 18) are as follows:
1. Indonesia: 180.11 million
2. United States: 153.12 million
3. Brazil: 130.84 million
Note: While China doesn’t make this list, it’s only because TikTok goes by a different name for Chinese users. There, the Douyin app (also owned by parent company ByteDance) boasts more than 766.5 million daily active users.
7. How popular is TikTok compared to other social media?
Although TikTok has enjoyed rapid growth, it still has a way to go to catch up with many of the other social media giants. As of 2025, TikTok is the fifth-most-popular social network globally (beating out WeChat), ranked by number of active users:
Facebook: 3.070 billion users

WhatsApp: 3 billion users
YouTube: 2.580 billion users
TikTok: 1.990 billion users
WeChat: 1.410 billion users
Given TikTok’s rate of growth, it could overtake competitors in the coming years.
8. How much time do TikTok users spend on the platform by age group?
Here’s how much time TikTok users spend on TikTok per day, according to their age group:
18- to 24-year-olds: 76 minutes
